rounds.proof_sketch: With size=262144, num_blocks=257, block 256 has threads with idx>=262144. These enter the else branch. For elem_idx=262144: original (elem_idx<size) is FALSE, mutant (elem_idx<=size) is TRUE. Mutant performs out-of-bounds access to input[262144]/output[262144], but valid output[0:262143] remains identical.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary condition from '<' to '<=' in the else branch of the vectorized kernel. With the fixed input shape [16, 16384] producing 262144 elements and 257 blocks launched, the last block's threads enter the else branch with idx=262144. The mutated condition allows elem_idx=262144 (one past the valid range), causing out-of-bounds memory access. However, this out-of-bounds write affects output[262144], which is beyond the valid tensor bounds. The torch.allclose comparison only examines the 262144 valid output elements (indices 0-262143), all of which are computed identically by both versions. Thus, the behavioral difference exists but cannot be observed through the comparison mechanism.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract because the mutation only affects out-of-bounds memory operations at index 262144, which falls outside the valid tensor comparison range. No value-level input can make this difference observable through torch.allclose on the valid output elements.
rounds.recommendations: Add explicit bounds checking with assertions or consider using tools like CUDA-MEMCHECK/compute-sanitizer to detect out-of-bounds accesses during testing. Also consider adding a test that verifies the kernel doesn't write beyond valid memory bounds, perhaps by padding the output buffer and checking the padding remains unchanged.
